summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all eight paragraphs of the selected Greek working source. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the Son’s priority and counselor relationship, the visionary identifications, and the exclusive entry requirements without adding doctrinal conditions. The simplified edition retains these assertions despite shortening the dialogue. The notes distinguish the editorially supplied verb and conjectural readings from reported Athos alternatives and appropriately limit the fragmentary evidence. Acceptance concerns fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure of the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify editions, or establish exhaustive collation.
